notice: EvoPilot identified modifications of OWLAPI 5.5.1 TurtleParser, JavaCharStream and TurtleParserTokenManager: separately rename derived classes; instrument existing semantic actions with optional raw UTF-16 source handles; decode IRIREF UCHAR escapes once from original input; validate generic RFC 3987 IRI-reference grammar and apply strict RFC 3986 section 5.2 base resolution through owned RDFIRI. Cache by resolved absolute identifier so successive BASE directives cannot reuse earlier relative resolutions; retain current BASE dependencies, including relative BASE chains. Validate QName-generated absolute identifiers without applying IRIREF resolution to prefixed-name concatenation. No percent decoding, syntax/scheme normalization, identifier repair, DNS/TLD or numeric port policy. Source-disabled parsing uses the same corrections without a collector or location budgets. Original classes and factories are not replaced. Unchanged source comments/notices are retained. Retain exact archive, recipe, derived and owned sources with source/license evidence; this is neither an unmodified upstream release nor license acceptance. The owned LocatedTurtleParser now delegates Turtle 1.1 lexical parsing to the separately pinned RDF4J 5.0.2 runtime and retains original source intervals through an owned subclass. Historical OWLAPI-derived parser classes remain separately attributable; they are not the active Turtle semantic path. No upstream RDF4J class is replaced.
reason: Correct evidenced IRI-reference grammar, relative/base resolution and cross-BASE cache defects against independent RFC3986/3987 and W3C Turtle oracles; do not preserve an upstream defect merely to retain parity. Keep exact original source spans, actual lexical dependencies and one-pass escape decoding. Source occurrence records alone do not establish complete RDF-to-OWL provenance. Preserve Unicode, percent spelling, case and empty components; syntax does not authorize network access.
acceptance: Actual parser event/ontology parity, exact Unicode offsets, resource limits, source-set mapper integration and formal source-fragment acceptance remain required.
